artworks.title: Hercules on the Pyre
artworks.description: Louvre INV 538: Reni's Mantuan cycle ends with Heracles on the funeral pile — the poisoned shirt's agony staged as monumental nude stoicism before the flames that will make him a god.

artworks.title: The Apotheosis of Hercules
artworks.description: Versailles Salon d'Hercule ceiling: after Oeta's pyre, Hercules is received on Olympus by Jupiter and Juno — the death that becomes godhead painted as Rococo triumph.

artworks.title: The Apotheosis of Hercules
artworks.description: Coypel's oil restages the cloud-borne ascent: the labourer of Trachis and Oeta lifted among the immortals — Hesiod's Hebe-wedding afterlife in French classical colour.

artworks.title: Nessus and Deianira
artworks.description: Simonet's academic canvas: the centaur seizes Deianira at the Evenus — the dying deceit that furnishes the poisoned 'love-charm' and seals Heracles' pyre years later.

music.title: Hercules
music.description: Handel's musical drama of the homecoming centres on Dejanira's jealousy, driving toward the poisoned robe and one of the great mad scenes of the baroque stage — Sophocles' Trachiniae as oratorio theatre.

popCulture.title: Trachiniae
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' Women of Trachis — Deianira's poisoned shirt and Heracles' pyre on Oeta as tragedy's death of the hero.

popCulture.title: Heracles
popCulture.description: The shirt of Nessus and the pyre that makes a god — Heracles' end remains as famous as his labours.

popCulture.title: Deianira
popCulture.description: The wife who meant to keep love and sent death — Deianira's name is bound forever to the hero's last agony.
